accuracy.evidence: Every sum in the lab, practice and challenge was recomputed (46 + 7 = 53, 38 + 5 = 43, 38 + 40 = 78, 57→60 is 3, 82→90 is 8, 26→30 is 4, 58 + 6 = 58 + 2 + 4 = 60 + 4 = 64, 29 + 5 = 34, 64 + 30 = 94) and the parameterised items were checked at the corners of their ranges by the items gate. Strategy wording checked against CCSS 1.NBT.4 (place-value strategies, two-digit + one-digit and + multiple of 10) and the NC Year 2 addition statements and non-statutory guidance on partitioning and bridging through ten.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented early-number errors: writing digits side by side (413, 295; tag join), staying in the same decade (46 + 7 = 43; split prediction, m5, tag stay), adding tens as ones (38 + 40 = 42; the '4 ones' card in the tens step, p5, tag ones), jumping by the ones digit instead of its bond to 10 (from 57 jumping 7; gap step feedback, tag digit), and overshooting the next ten (tag past).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagadd100 is built around bridging: scissors dragged along a row of ones cubes set the partition, and the first number-line hop turns green only when it lands on a multiple of ten; ten rods dragged into a dashed box raise only the tens digit; a dot dragged along a 20-wide line to the next ten; sums sorted by which digit changes; tiles completing 58 + 6 = 58 + 2 + 4 = 60 + 4 = 64. flagtenjump is 10 more/10 less on a hundred square and flagregroup is the column method within 1000; the distinct gate measured at most a few percent overlap with any lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners find the rule before the text states it: a cut at 2 for 46 + 7 gives a hop to 48 with the message that it is not a whole ten, and only the 4/3 cut turns the hops green; the tens counter shows the 8 ones never move while the tens digit climbs 3→7; jumping 7 from 57 is named as using the ones digit; the six sorted sums end up split into tens, ones and both, which states the place-value pattern.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options: 'still in the forties' for 46 + 7 (the stay-in-decade error), 'both digits' / 'only the ones digit' for 38 + 40, and 'yes, both add three' for 52 + 3 versus 52 + 30. Each is tested by the task straight after, and the reveal line names the right answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating questions (46 + 7, 38 + 40, gap from 57, which digit changes for 52 + 30, why split 6 into 2 and 4, 29 + 5, 64 + 30). Wrong options carry tags stay, join, ones, tens, digit, past, both and split, each with its own message naming the slip, e.g. '7 is the ones digit. The jump is the number that makes 10 with 7, which is 3.'

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes the kid and adult readability limits. Kid sentences are short and use concrete numbers ('46 needs 4 more to make 50. Then add the 3 that are left.'). Curriculum words place value, tens, ones, bridge, number bond and multiple of ten are used in the adult text and shown, not just named, in the lab. Young-mode buttons are 56 px tall.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: do not count in ones, bridge through ten, add tens, bonds to 10. Adult: standards and key words, why bridging works and how it links to written recording, five named mistakes, then exactly what the lab does. No filler pattern matched and the 12% overlap gate passed against the within-20, within-1000 and 10-more lessons.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android dark, iPhone 13 light and desktop screenshots after Show me. Fixed from the first pass: the tens-step title overlapped the +10 hop labels (number line moved to 25% height), the sort boxes clipped 'Only the tens digit changes' (canvas now shows 'Tens / Ones / Both change', full wording stays on the buttons), the equation rows collided with the hops (canvas made taller, line and tiles moved down), and finished steps now keep the last number line visible instead of a blank panel.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin: 'Move the cut left/right' and 'Make the jumps', 'Add a ten rod' / 'Add 4 ones', 'One less' / 'One more' / 'Check the jump', one button per sort box labelled with the current sum, and one button per number tile. The canvas aria-label and live region carry each message. walk.cjs passed axe WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors; real pointer drags were tested for the cut, the ten rods and the gap dot.
